note: One body is byte-exact and four functions of the SDK's runtime are byte-identical in the retail executable. A build is not qualified on one function: the profile below is provisional until it holds on more.

compiler.sources: the Cell OS Lv-2 toolchain sources, as published by sagemono/ps3gcc at the tag toolchain-src-2.7.0-GCC411
compiler.built_in: a Debian jessie container with a period-appropriate host compiler
compiler.note: The toolchain is a tool. It is built by the contributor and is never published; the repository holds the written result only. The stamp of the build is the SDK 2.7.0 one, while the retail program was built with the SDK 4.0: the compiler is the same GCC 4.1.1, and the difference of the stamp does not show in the code.

flags.note: The flag that matters is -mno-save-restore-tocbase: without it the compiler keeps a TOC base and a back chain in the frame, which the retail code does not have. At -O2 the same function differs by two instructions: the compiler restores the stack pointer before the link register, where the retail code does the opposite.

runtime_cross_check.note: The retail executable links libgcc statically, so the SDK's own runtime is in the text. Every function of our build of the runtime that is found in the retail text is byte-identical to the one the game runs. No source has to be written for that check.
